title: Building a Point You Can Hold
description: Watch how a VR-interactive point builds up from a single Vector3 to 271 lines of embodied mathematics.

capture_leaks.duration: Point_Trace — a point has no history until you draw its trail
capture_leaks.relation: Point_Line — a single point has no neighbors, no between-space
capture_leaks.size: Point_Triangle — a point has no extent; three points begin area
capture_leaks.identity: qfeplaboratory — Vector3(1,0,0) is never the same point twice; identity requires time
capture_leaks.continuity: cellularautomata, noise — points are discrete; the space between them is invisible

limit: A point is pure position. It holds no history, no neighbor, no size, no persistence. Each of these silences is a door to the next map.

stages.title: A point is just data
stages.thinking: Before rendering, before interaction — a point is a Vector3. Three floats. An address in space. Everything that follows is just making this address visible and touchable.
stages.code:
# A point is pure position — nothing more, nothing less
var point_position: Vector3 = Vector3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)

# Three numbers. That's all a point is.
# x = 1.0 (right)
# y = 0.5 (up)
# z = 0.0 (forward)
#
# But nobody can see three floats.
# We need to give this address a body.

stages.title: Give it a body
stages.thinking: Data needs a body to be seen. We create a sphere mesh — small, glowing, cyan — so the point has physical presence in 3D space. The mesh is not the point. The mesh is how we see the point.
stages.code:
extends Node3D

func _ready() -> void:
	# Create a tiny sphere so the point is visible
	var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere = SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = 0.03
	sphere.height = 0.06
	mesh_instance.mesh = sphere
	add_child(mesh_instance)
	
	# Make it glow so it's visible in dark scenes
	var material = StandardMaterial3D.new()
	material.emission_enabled = true
	material.emission = Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0)
	material.emission_energy_multiplier = 2.0
	mesh_instance.material_override = material

stages.title: Show the coordinates
stages.thinking: A visible sphere shows where, but not what. We add a Label3D billboard that displays the live coordinates — the numbers that define this point's identity. The label updates every frame because position can change.
stages.code:
extends Node3D

var _position_label: Label3D

func _ready() -> void:
	var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere = SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = 0.03
	mesh_instance.mesh = sphere
	add_child(mesh_instance)
	
	# Billboard label showing coordinates
	_position_label = Label3D.new()
	_position_label.billboard = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
	_position_label.font_size = 32
	_position_label.position.y = 0.08
	mesh_instance.add_child(_position_label)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if _position_label:
		var pos = global_position
		_position_label.text = "(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]

stages.title: Make it grabbable
stages.thinking: Now the point has a body and a name. But you can only look at it. By extending XRToolsPickable instead of Node3D, the point becomes something your hand can grab. Your hand writes new coordinates 90 times per second — position is produced by embodied action.

stages.title: Draw distance to origin
stages.thinking: When you hold the point, a glowing line stretches from your hand to (0,0,0). Distance stops being a number — it becomes a visible, physical thing that grows and shrinks as you move. The line is a CylinderMesh created once and reused (no per-frame allocation).
stages.code:
@tool
extends XRToolsPickable

@export var line_color: Color = Color(0.3, 0.8, 1.0, 0.7)
@export var line_width: float = 0.003
@export var origin_point: Vector3 = Vector3.ZERO

var _is_held := false
var _line_mesh_instance: MeshInstance3D
var _line_material: StandardMaterial3D
var _line_cylinder: CylinderMesh
var _last_line_distance: float = -1.0
var _position_label: Label3D

func _ready() -> void:
	super()
	_setup_line_to_origin()
	_position_label = get_node_or_null("MeshInstance3D/Label3D")
	if _position_label:
		_position_label.visible = false
	picked_up.connect(_on_picked_up)
	dropped.connect(_on_dropped)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if _is_held:
		_update_line_to_origin()
		_update_position_label()

func _setup_line_to_origin() -> void:
	# Create line mesh once — reuse every frame
	_line_mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
	_line_mesh_instance.name = "LineToOrigin"
	_line_mesh_instance.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	add_child(_line_mesh_instance)
	
	_line_cylinder = CylinderMesh.new()
	_line_cylinder.top_radius = line_width
	_line_cylinder.bottom_radius = line_width
	_line_cylinder.radial_segments = 6
	_line_cylinder.rings = 1
	_line_mesh_instance.mesh = _line_cylinder
	
	_line_material = StandardMaterial3D.new()
	_line_material.albedo_color = line_color
	_line_material.emission_enabled = true
	_line_material.emission = line_color
	_line_material.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
	_line_material.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
	_line_mesh_instance.material_override = _line_material
	_line_mesh_instance.visible = false

func _update_line_to_origin() -> void:
	var current_pos: Vector3 = global_position
	var direction: Vector3 = origin_point - current_pos
	var distance: float = direction.length()
	
	if distance < 0.001:
		_line_mesh_instance.visible = false
		return
	
	_line_mesh_instance.visible = true
	_line_cylinder.height = distance
	
	# Position at midpoint, rotate to face origin
	var midpoint = (current_pos + origin_point) / 2.0
	_line_mesh_instance.global_position = midpoint
	var up = Vector3.UP
	if abs(direction.normalized().dot(up)) > 0.99:
		up = Vector3.RIGHT
	_line_mesh_instance.look_at(origin_point, up)
	_line_mesh_instance.rotate_object_local(Vector3.RIGHT, PI / 2.0)

func _on_picked_up(_pickable) -> void:
	_is_held = true
	if _position_label:
		_position_label.visible = true
	if _line_mesh_instance:
		_line_mesh_instance.visible = true

func _on_dropped(_pickable) -> void:
	_is_held = false
	if _position_label:
		_position_label.visible = false
	if _line_mesh_instance:
		_line_mesh_instance.visible = false

func _update_position_label() -> void:
	if not _position_label:
		return
	var pos = global_position
	_position_label.text = "(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]

stages.title: Add body feedback
stages.thinking: Seeing is not enough. The body needs to feel the interaction. We add three feedback channels: a material glow when held (magenta emission), a synthesized 880Hz tone on pickup (not a file — pure math), and haptic pulses through the controller. The body learns before the mind names what it learned.

stages.title: Cycle display formats
stages.thinking: Each pickup cycles the coordinate display through four formats: decimal, labeled, Vector3 syntax, and hidden. This isn't decoration — it's pedagogy. The learner sees that the same position has multiple valid representations. The point doesn't change. Only how we name it changes.
stages.code:
var _display_format_index: int = 2  # Start at 2 so first pickup shows format 0

func _on_picked_up(_pickable) -> void:
	# Cycle through display formats on each pickup
	_display_format_index = (_display_format_index + 1) % 4
	# ... glow, sound, haptic ...

func _update_position_label() -> void:
	if not _position_label:
		return
	var pos = global_position
	match _display_format_index:
		0:
			_position_label.visible = true
			_position_label.text = "(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]
		1:
			_position_label.visible = true
			_position_label.text = "(x:%.2f, y:%.2f, z:%.2f)" % [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]
		2:
			_position_label.visible = true
			_position_label.text = "Vector3(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]
		3:
			_position_label.visible = false

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The code is complete. Now it learns to speak about itself. The @identity block is not documentation — it's self-knowledge. 'A coordinate is a measurement from origin — hold the point, feel the measurement.' The code knows what it is, why it exists, and what truth it carries.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: p = (x, y, z) — a position you can hold in your hand
# desire: learner feels coordinates as embodied distance, not abstract numbers
# critical_parameter: the live line drawn to (0,0,0) while held
# triggers: pickup cycles through 4 coordinate display formats
# emerges: haptic pulse as format-change event — the body learns before the mind
# needs: Label3D [has], grabbable (XRToolsPickable) [has]
# relationships: depends on origin; used alongside static_point
# truth: a coordinate is a measurement from origin — hold the point, feel the measurement
